\begin{quote}
\textbf{Cournot Revisited:} Consider the Cournot duopoly model in which two firms, 1 and 2, simultaneously choose the quantities they supply, \(q_1\) and \(q_2\). The price each will face is determined by the market demand function \(p(q_1, q_2) = a - b(q_1 + q_2)\). Each firm has a probability \(\mu\) of having a marginal unit cost of \(c_L\) and a probability \(1 - \mu\) of having a marginal unit cost of \(c_H\). These probabilities are common knowledge, but the true type is revealed only to each firm individually. Solve for the Bayesian Nash equilibrium.
\end{quote}
